notes: This file is the cross-language EIP-712 contract for BitcoinOwnershipOracle. The five attestor
services and packages/protocol-sdk MUST reproduce every value here byte for byte. An
implementation that builds a different digest does not produce an invalid signature — it
produces a signature for a DIFFERENT message, which the oracle simply will not recognise. That
failure is silent from the signer's point of view, which is exactly why it is pinned here.
EVERY EXPECTED VALUE WAS OBSERVED BY RUNNING SOLIDITY, NEVER HAND-DERIVED. The domain
separator and all four digests were produced by the real BitcoinOwnershipOracle runtime
bytecode executing at the pinned chainId and verifyingContract below, and are re-derived on
every test run (see test_PinnedDomainSeparatorMatchesTheContract and
test_PinnedDigestsMatchTheContract).
THE STRUCT HASHES COMPOSE WITH hashing-vectors.json. Three of the four message instances reuse
that file's hashStruct fixtures field for field, so the two files chain together:
digest == keccak256(0x1901 || domainSeparator || structHash)
A drift in either file therefore fails both suites rather than neither.
THE TXIDS ARE SYNTHETIC. They are structurally valid 32-byte values chosen for reproducibility.
None is a real Bitcoin transaction and none identifies a real Bitcoin Puppets inscription.
Byte order: every txid is big-endian / RPC display order, the order a block explorer shows.
uint256 and uint64 values are strings because they exceed the safe integer range of JSON.
TRUST BOUNDARY: none of these hashes verifies a Bitcoin fact, and the oracle that consumes them
cannot verify one either. Bitcoin facts are asserted by a 3-of-5 quorum of independent attestor
operators. This is an attested settlement system, not a trustless bridge.

ownershipAttestation.note: IDENTICAL FIELDS to hashStruct/OwnershipAttestation in hashing-vectors.json, so the two files chain. This is a HASHING vector, not a semantically valid attestation: purpose 0 (PAID_EVM_MINT) with payoutMode 1 (EVM) would be rejected by BitcoinOwnershipOracle's payout-shape check because btcPayoutScriptHash and sellerSats are non-zero. Every field is deliberately non-zero — zero fields hide field-ordering bugs. Use ownershipAttestationSelfCast for a vector that both hashes correctly AND passes verifyOwnership.

ownershipAttestationSelfCast.note: purpose 2 is AuthorizationPurpose.SELF_CAST; payoutMode 0 is PayoutMode.NONE. This is the SEMANTICALLY VALID vector: a self-cast moves no money, so every payout and monetary field is zero, which is exactly what BitcoinOwnershipOracle enforces. The same zero-payout shape is required for ROOT_BIND (purpose 3) and ROOT_INVALIDATE (purpose 4).

bitcoinPaymentAttestation.note: IDENTICAL FIELDS to hashStruct/BitcoinPaymentAttestation in hashing-vectors.json. derivedPaymentOutputKey is PuppetHashing.paymentOutputKey(bitcoinTxid, outputIndex) and is the value the oracle marks consumed alongside the digest; it is quoted here (and pinned in hashing-vectors.json as paymentOutputKey/fixturePayment) so a settlement service can pre-check isPaymentOutputKeyConsumed before broadcasting a Bitcoin payment.

rootSpendAttestation.note: IDENTICAL FIELDS to hashStruct/RootSpendAttestation in hashing-vectors.json.

encodings: 64 bytes: EIP-2098 compact, r (32) || vs (32), where the top bit of vs carries yParity.
signatureRules.ordering: The signatures array MUST be sorted strictly ascending by RECOVERED SIGNER ADDRESS, not by signature bytes. This single rule rejects duplicate signers, makes the accepted form of a quorum canonical, and lets the oracle verify in one pass. Sorting the signature bytes instead orders by ECDSA output, which has no relationship to the signer, and will be rejected.
signatureRules.malleability: An upper-half s value is rejected. Signing libraries must produce a low-s signature (every mainstream library does). The compact 64-byte form cannot express an upper-half s at all, since that bit carries the recovery id.
signatureRules.freshness: attestorEpoch and policyVersion must EQUAL the live values from BitcoinAttestorRegistry.quorumContext() at execution time, and deadline must be >= block.timestamp (the expiry second itself is still valid). Any registry mutation bumps the epoch and invalidates every in-flight signature; re-request attestations rather than retrying.
signatureRules.singleUse: Each digest is consumable exactly once, permanently. A Bitcoin payment output, keyed by PuppetHashing.paymentOutputKey(txid, vout), is likewise consumable exactly once across the whole protocol.

crossLanguageChecklist: Build the domain separator from the four domain fields, using the LIVE chainId and the deployed oracle address — never the placeholder above.
Build encodeData as the typehash followed by one 32-byte word per field, in the frozen order. Do not use packed encoding, and do not sort or omit fields.
Left-pad every txid and script hash to 32 bytes and keep display (big-endian) byte order.
Sign the digest directly. Do NOT apply the personal_sign / EIP-191 prefix on top of it.
Sort the collected signatures by recovered signer address, ascending, before submitting.
Re-run this file's four vectors on every release of the SDK and of each attestor service.
